races.title: State Senate, District 18
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Haseeb Fatmi
cands.bio: Attorney (of counsel at Ogletree Deakins) and adjunct professor who teaches trial advocacy at Campbell Law School. Elected to the Wake Forest Board of Commissioners in November 2025. Appointed to North Carolina Senate District 18 in May 2026 to succeed Terence Everitt. UNC-Chapel Hill and Fordham Law graduate.

endorsements.text: Per his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, he lists endorsements from the Sierra Club, North Carolina League of Conservation Voters, Planned Parenthood Votes! South Atlantic, Reproductive Freedom for All, the Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee, Run for Something, the North Carolina Association of Educators, Indian American Impact Fund, Climate Cabinet, Building Blue, Equality NC PAC, New American Leaders Action Fund and NCAAT in Action.

cands.gaps: We could not find his city of birth. We found no record of specific actions he took as a Wake Forest commissioner or in the state Senate, and no sponsored-bill list. We found no stated position from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, restrictions on out-of-state or institutional land buyers, immigration enforcement or H-1B, or abortion. His campaign site says only that he opposes special-interest influence and supports tax relief for working families, without naming specific pledges. His work history comes from his campaign site and Wikipedia, and we found no independent reporting to confirm it.

local.label: Roots 100: He says he was born and raised in North Carolina and attended Wake County public schools, and Wikipedia and his campaign site say the same.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Attorney since 2012 (trial attorney, Social Security Administration, federal bankruptcy judge's clerk, now of counsel at a Raleigh firm), adjunct law professor, Wake Forest town commissioner from late 2025, and appointed state senator since May 2026.
qual.why: He has local elected office and a long law career, which fits the middle band. His state legislative service is only a few months old, so he does not reach the top band.
qual.label: He has local elected office and a long law career, which fits the middle band. His state legislative service is only a few months old, so he does not reach the top band.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: His campaign site says he will work to protect natural areas such as Smith Creek and Kerr Lake and to ensure overdevelopment does not come at the expense of local communities.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he supports more funding for local law enforcement, fair pay and retention benefits, and the same for correctional and highway patrol officers.

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site says he supports commonsense gun safety laws, with no specifics given.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

roots.summary: He says he was born and raised in North Carolina and attended Wake County public schools, and Wikipedia and his campaign site say the same.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Campaign site: he says he will work to protect natural areas like Smith Creek and Kerr Lake and ensure that overdevelopment does not come at the expense of local communities, citing conflicts between developers and local communities over natural and green spaces.

cands.name: Chris Stock
cands.bio: Republican candidate for North Carolina Senate District 18 (Granville and Wake Counties) in 2026. He says he grew up in Wake Forest and worked in the North Carolina General Assembly and for State Senator Brent Jackson. He won the March 2026 Republican primary.

endorsements.text: Per his own Ballotpedia survey response, he lists endorsements from Sen. Brent Jackson, Sen. Bill Rabon, former Lt. Gov. Dan Forest and Agriculture Commissioner Steve Troxler. Ballotpedia says it did not independently identify any endorsements.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Chris Stock was born or when his family settled in North Carolina. We found no job titles, dates or employers for his General Assembly and Senator Brent Jackson staff work beyond his own summary. He has held no elected office, so there is no record of actions in office. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, immigration or H-1B, gun laws, abortion, or school vouchers and charters. We found no stated position on a ban on investor purchases of homes. We found no news coverage or controversies about him. We found no source, beyond his own survey answer, confirming his endorsements.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign site says he was raised in Wake Forest as the son of a small business owner and substitute teacher, and attended Wake County Public Schools; his birthplace is not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: By his own account he has worked in the North Carolina General Assembly and for State Senator Brent Jackson, where he says he learned to craft legislation and budgets. He has held no elected office.
qual.why: Legislative staff experience puts him in the middle band. The sources give no job titles, dates or length of service, and he has no elected record. The staff work is self-reported.
qual.label: Legislative staff experience puts him in the middle band. The sources give no job titles, dates or length of service, and he has no elected record. The staff work is self-reported.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Says he is a strong advocate for legislation that limits property tax increases that threaten to price neighbors out of their homes.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says he supports legislation that preserves farmland from development.

land-for-floridians.evidence: Says he supports legislation that keeps North Carolina's food supply out of the hands of foreign adversaries. This is stated in the context of farmland and agriculture.

back-police-order.evidence: Says he supports ending cashless bail, fully supporting police and giving emergency services the funding they need.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says he is a strong advocate for increasing teacher pay. He did not state a position on vouchers or charters.

prio.label: Matches 5 of 5 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 5 only promised
